findings.issue_text: [BUG] The script resolves the env file as the CWD-relative path `../.env` (line 5) and never cd's to its own directory, so invoking it the natural way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) targets `<parent-of-repo>/.env` instead of the repository's .env. Run from the repo root, the script `touch`es (line 64) and then writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into a .env outside the repository, prints '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in ../.env', and the repo's real .env is never modified — the webhook URL silently never takes effect and a stray .env is created above the checkout.

[BUG] `sed -i '' -E "s|...|...|"` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; GNU sed does not attach `''` to `-i` (optional short-option arguments must be attached), so on Linux `''` is parsed as the sed script and the substitution expression as an input filename. On Linux the script errors with "sed: can't read s|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...|: No such file or directory" and rewrites the env file in place under an empty script, leaving the existing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL value unchanged — the in-place update no-ops on every non-macOS dev environment.

[ADVISORY] The handler unconditionally instantiates the real CalendarCacheRepository and runs a calendarCache groupBy on every connectedCalendars request with no calendar-cache feature gate, bypassing the disabled-mode contract the module's own CalendarCacheRepositoryMock encodes ('Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled'). Deployments with calendar-cache disabled — where every other cache operation no-ops through the mock — now pay an extra DB query per fetch of this frequently-loaded route, and the module has two divergent behaviors for the same feature state.

[ADVISORY] The handler deletes cache rows via raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` instead of the existing `ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential`, whose mock no-ops when calendar-cache is disabled. A second, ungated deletion path now exists outside the repository layer: when the calendar-cache feature is disabled the endpoint still performs live DB deletes, and any future change to cache-deletion semantics in the repository must be independently replicated here.

[ADVISORY] `dev:cron` now invokes tsx through `npx` without tsx being added to any package.json in this diff, making resolution depend on tsx happening to be installed in the workspace rather than on the yarn lockfile. On a checkout where tsx is not installed, `yarn dev:cron` makes npx fetch an unpinned latest tsx from the public registry at run time (network required, version drift, first-run 'Ok to proceed?' install prompt in a TTY), so the script's behavior varies per machine instead of being pinned.

[ADVISORY] The new deleteCache mutation ships with no test, and its only authorization is the `userId: user.id` clause in the findFirst at lines 18-21. A regression that drops or mis-scopes the userId clause would let any authenticated user delete another user's CalendarCache rows (forcing cache rebuilds and breaking the cache-status display), and no test in this diff would fail.

[BUG] The diff ships new destructive server-side logic (deleteCache.handler with its ownership check and calendarCache.deleteMany, plus the new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy) with no test anywhere in the diff. Scanned the diff for test-shaped files: none exist (the only test-named artifact is scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, a manual tunnelmole setup script, and calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts is a no-op DI mock with zero assertions). Because both files are new, no out-of-diff test can cover them either. Specific unverified assertions: a non-owner's credentialId is rejected, an owned credential's cache rows are actually removed, and the groupBy maps _max.updatedAt per credential. A regression in the userId: user.id filter would let any authenticated user wipe another user's availability cache, and nothing in CI would catch it.

[BUG] The cache section is gated only on isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt and ignores delegationCredentialId, so members connected via a domain-wide-delegation credential are offered 'Delete cached data', but deleteCache.handler.ts:17-22 resolves the credential with userId: user.id, which an org-level delegation credential never satisfies. For every org member using domain-wide delegation who has cache rows (the shared delegation credential's CalendarCache entries), the dropdown shows the delete action and clicking it always throws 'Credential not found or access denied', surfacing the 'Error deleting cache' toast; the advertised action is permanently broken for that user segment, with no working alternative path in the UI.

[BUG] The handler throws a plain Error('Credential not found or access denied') instead of a TRPCError, so tRPC maps an expected authorization miss to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR. Clients receive a 500 (with the message stripped in production) for what is a 4xx-shaped outcome, and error monitoring fills with server-error noise every time a user hits the not-found/not-owned path (including the delegation case above), instead of a distinguishable NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code.

[BUG] The script uses BSD-only `sed -i ''` (line 68), which fails on GNU/Linux because the empty string is parsed as the script argument, and ENV_FILE='../.env' (line 5) resolves against the caller's CWD. On Linux the substitution errors and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated, silently leaving the previous (likely stale) tunnel URL in .env so webhook verification fails; and invoking the script from the repo root instead of scripts/ creates or edits a .env outside the repository.

[ADVISORY] The handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly and runs getCacheStatusByCredentialIds unconditionally on every connectedCalendars request, with no check of whether calendar-cache is enabled — the disabled mode the repository mock (calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts, 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled') exists to represent. Deployments with calendar-cache disabled pay an extra groupBy query on every settings-page load for a feature they don't use, and the disabled-mode mock cannot stand in for this call path, so any unit test of connectedCalendars.handler is forced against real Prisma instead of the repository seam the package provides.

[ADVISORY] fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now runs an unconditional updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) whose only possible effect is Prisma's @updatedAt side effect on SelectedCalendar.updatedAt — a field nothing in this diff reads, alongside the parallel dead additions of updatedAt/googleChannelId to the UserWithCalendars picks (getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21-30) and the UserRepository select (user.ts:899-900). Every cache refresh pays a multi-row UPDATE to maintain an unread signal (the dropdown's 'Last updated' comes from CalendarCache.updatedAt via the handler enrichment, and CalendarSwitch receives only externalId/destination/credentialId/eventTypeId/delegationCredentialId), every user-with-calendars fetch ships two extra columns per selected calendar, and the two same-named 'updatedAt' signals diverge after deleteCache (CalendarCache rows deleted, SelectedCalendar.updatedAt left stale), misleading future readers about which one is the cache status.

[ADVISORY] disableConnectionModification is now passed into CredentialActionsDropdown whose hasCache branch ignores it, so the flag no longer guarantees an action-free card: Google credentials with cache rows render a destructive 'Delete cached data' control even when connection modification is disabled (the old code rendered no actions at all in that mode). Platform embedders who set disableConnectionModification to freeze the connected-calendar card get a new user-facing destructive action after upgrade with no flag to suppress it, widening the flag's contract silently; the same applies to delegation-credential cards, which previously rendered nothing.

[ADVISORY] The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') in an otherwise fully localized component that uses useLocale/t for all its strings. Non-English users always see US-style month/day dates for the cache status regardless of their app locale, an i18n regression on a newly added user-visible string.

[BUG] The availability cache-refresh path now performs an unconditional multi-row UPDATE of SelectedCalendar (updateManyByCredentialId called with an empty data payload), but no code in this diff consumes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt — the cache status shown to users is computed from CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Every Google Calendar cache refresh pays an extra write across all of the credential's SelectedCalendars for nothing the feature reads; if out-of-diff logic orders or filters by SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, its semantics silently change, and the empty `{}` payload means the call's only possible effect is Prisma's implicit @updatedAt handling — invisible at the call site and version-sensitive.

[BUG] A 79-line Tunnelmole webhook-tunnel developer script is added to a calendar-cache-status feature PR; nothing in the feature (cache status display, deleteCache endpoint, CalendarCache.updatedAt column) touches webhook URLs or tunneling. Unrelated infrastructure ships and is maintained under this feature's banner — the script mutates the developer's ../.env (GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL), depends on an external third-party service (tunnelmole), and uses macOS-only `sed -i ''` syntax that fails on GNU sed, and no requirement in this PR calls for any of it.

[BUG] The cache 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded en-US Intl.DateTimeFormat instead of the viewing user's locale. Every non-English user sees US-style date/time (e.g. '6/30/25, 3:04 PM') in an otherwise fully localized UI; the app's locale tooling (useLocale/dayjs) is bypassed on this new surface.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error for the expected not-found/not-owned case instead of a TRPCError, so tRPC maps it to a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with the message redacted in production. An expected 4xx-class outcome (wrong or non-owned credentialId) is logged and monitored as a server error, and the client receives an opaque 500 rather than a distinguishable not-found/forbidden response.

[ADVISORY] The new authed mutation's only authorization is the userId filter inside deleteCacheHandler, and no test in the diff covers the handler, the new groupBy repository method, or the connectedCalendars enrichment. A regression that drops or weakens the userId filter would let any authenticated user delete CalendarCache rows for arbitrary credentials (forcing live Google availability calls at scale), and nothing in CI would catch it.

[ADVISORY] updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the SelectedCalendar Pick type (forcing the matching select addition in UserRepository) but no code in the diff reads either field — the cache status comes from CalendarCache.updatedAt instead. Every user fetch pulls and serializes two unused columns per selected calendar to tRPC clients; the dead plumbing indicates an abandoned per-calendar status design left inside the PR.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of obtaining it through the calendar-cache DI switch whose disabled-state mock this same diff extends. Deployments with calendar cache disabled still pay a calendar_cache groupBy on every connectedCalendars fetch, and the mock's new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is dead code on the only path added for this feature.

[ADVISORY] findMany is refactored to drop the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` conformance assertion with no connection to the cache-status feature. An unexplained drive-by change to shared repository code widens the feature diff and removes the explicit compile-time assertion that assembled args match Prisma's findMany input, making the next change to this method harder to review.

[ADVISORY] The component re-implements the disconnect flow (viewer.credentials.delete mutation, success/error toasts, confirm dialog, cache invalidations) in parallel to the existing DisconnectIntegration component, which remains in use on other surfaces. Two hand-maintained copies of the disconnect behavior can drift — a future change to invalidation or error handling in one will silently miss the other.

[ADVISORY] The migration backfills every existing CalendarCache row's updatedAt with the migration-time NOW(), which is exactly the value the new UI presents as 'Last updated'. After deploy, all pre-existing cache entries display the deploy timestamp as their last-updated time until they expire and are rewritten — a wrong status shown to users for up to the cache TTL.

[ADVISORY] The dev:cron script change from ts-node to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` is unrelated to the calendar-cache feature and touches nothing the feature uses. Untraceable tooling drift rides in the feature PR, and `npx tsx` resolves the runner outside the project's pinned script tooling (downloading it on demand if not installed), making the dev script's toolchain nondeterministic.

[BUG] The cache-refresh path records freshness by bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}), empty data relying on @updatedAt), but the PR's own status read path (getCacheStatusByCredentialIds) computes cacheUpdatedAt from CalendarCache.updatedAt — writer and reader are bound to two different tables, so the bump maintains a signal nothing in this diff reads. Every cache-miss availability fetch pays an extra updateMany (row locks on all of the credential's SelectedCalendar rows) whose result no consumer uses, and a failure in this bookkeeping write fails the availability call after the fetch already succeeded; meanwhile the 'Last updated' shown in the UI is derived from CalendarCache row writes, so the two freshness sources diverge (cache disabled → bump advances but UI shows nothing; 'Delete cached data' → UI clears while the bump persists), and any existing consumer of SelectedCalendar.updatedAt's row-change semantics silently gets 'last availability fetch of the credential' instead.

[BUG] For Google Workspace delegation connections the dropdown renders 'Delete cached data' (hasCache checks only integration type and cacheUpdatedAt, never delegationCredentialId), but deleteCache.handler's ownership filter userId: user.id can never match an org-owned delegation credential (userId is null), so the mutation always throws. Users with delegated (workspace) Google connections that have CalendarCache rows see a 'Delete cached data' action that fails on every click with 'Error deleting cache' (the handler's generic Error surfaces as a tRPC 500); cache for those connections can never be cleared from the UI.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache.handler bypasses the calendar-cache repository abstraction and calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, even though ICalendarCacheRepository already declares deleteManyByCredential (implemented and mocked) for exactly this operation. A second, parallel data-access path for CalendarCache: the disabled-cache mode the repository mock enforces (no-op + log) does not apply to this delete, and any future repository-level behavior (scoping, logging, channel cleanup) added to deleteManyByCredential will silently not cover this handler.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendars.handler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly instead of obtaining it through the selection mechanism the rest of the feature uses (interface + CalendarCacheRepositoryMock representing the disabled mode), so this read path has no disabled mode. Every connectedCalendars call queries the calendarCache table even when calendar-cache is disabled (the mock path every other cache operation respects is bypassed), leaving the feature with two inconsistent instantiation styles that will drift.

[ADVISORY] The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US') instead of the user's locale. Every non-en-US user sees US-format dates in the cache status dropdown; the component already has useLocale() in scope and the rest of the app localizes dates, so this surface silently ignores the user's locale setting.

[BUG] sed -i '' -E ... is BSD/macOS-only syntax; GNU sed on Linux parses '' as the sed script and the substitution expression as an input filename, so the in-place env update fails on Linux. A Linux developer running scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh gets a 'can't read s|GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...|' error and GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never written, so gcal webhooks silently keep pointing at the old tunnel URL while the script appears to have run.

[BUG] ENV_FILE='../.env' is resolved relative to the current working directory, not the script's location. Invoked the normal way from the repo root (./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh), the script creates/edits a .env one level ABOVE the repo, so the webhook URL never reaches the app's .env while the script prints '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL'.

[ADVISORY] updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select and the UserWithCalendars payload, but nothing in this diff consumes them — the handler computes cacheUpdatedAt from CalendarCache instead of the selected calendars' updatedAt. Every connectedCalendars response carries two extra per-calendar fields no client reads, and the schema now exposes two parallel freshness/watch signals (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt/googleChannelId vs CalendarCache.updatedAt) that invite the next developer to bind to the wrong one, as this PR's writer/reader split already does.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler authorizes via credential.userId = user.id, but CredentialActionsDropdown shows 'Delete cached data' for delegated Google credentials too (hasCache at CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69 never checks delegationCredentialId), and delegation credential rows are org-owned with userId null — so the findFirst at lines 17-22 finds nothing for every delegation credential. Every workspace user with a delegated Google calendar who clicks 'Delete cached data' gets the 'Error deleting cache' toast — the action this PR adds is permanently broken for the delegation segment, and each attempt is logged server-side as a 500.

[BUG] The cache-refresh write path updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (line 1024) while the feature's read path — connectedCalendars.handler -> getCacheStatusByCredentialIds — reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, so the new updateManyByCredentialId call has no consumer anywhere in this PR and adds an extra updateMany DB write to every calendar-cache refresh. Every availability refresh pays a write that changes nothing the UI displays — a leftover of an abandoned per-calendar design; for delegation credentials, one user's refresh rewrites the SelectedCalendar rows of every org member under that credential, and if any pre-existing consumer reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, its meaning is silently altered by this write.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendars.handler instantiates CalendarCacheRepository directly (line 28) instead of resolving ICalendarCacheRepository, bypassing the container binding that swaps in CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar-cache is disabled — the very mock this PR extends with getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. With calendar-cache disabled, every connectedCalendars call still queries the CalendarCache table, and tests that bind the mock never intercept this handler; the disabled-gate contract the repository layer exists to enforce is silently skipped.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache.handler throws a plain Error ('Credential not found or access denied', line 25) instead of a TRPCError, so tRPC surfaces it as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) rather than the 4xx the situation warrants. An expected, client-triggerable condition (foreign credentialId, or the delegation-credential case above) is reported and logged as a server error on every occurrence, polluting error monitoring and masking real 5xxs.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' Intl.DateTimeFormat (lines 89-92) instead of the viewer's locale, in an app that otherwise localizes every rendered date. Non-English users get US-style date formatting in the new cache-status UI from day one, inconsistent with every other timestamp surface in the product.

[ADVISORY] updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the SelectedCalendar Pick in the exported UserWithCalendars type (lines 22-29) and to UserRepository's select (packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899-900), but no code in this diff reads either field — the UI's cacheUpdatedAt comes from the CalendarCache groupBy instead. Inert fields are threaded through a shared exported type and a hot user query — dead weight from the abandoned per-calendar status design that the next reader must reverse-engineer and that connectedCalendars payloads carry indefinitely.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache.handler mutates CalendarCache via raw prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany (lines 28-30) even though ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential exists precisely to centralize cache mutations behind the enabled/disabled binding. A second parallel path for cache deletion that ignores the calendar-cache-disabled gate — when the feature is off the mutation still issues a DB delete, and future changes to cache-deletion semantics must be maintained in two places.

[ADVISORY] The new authz-bearing mutation (ownership check plus deleteMany, lines 13-33) ships with no test in this diff, and neither getCacheStatusByCredentialIds nor the dropdown's canDisconnect/hasCache gating is covered. A regression that drops the userId filter would let any authenticated user delete any credential's calendar-cache rows by iterating credentialIds — a silent authorization breakage nothing in CI would catch.

[ADVISORY] A 79-line Tunnelmole webhook-testing dev script — which also rewrites the developer's ../.env GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL — ships inside a PR whose stated objective is calendar cache status and actions, with nothing tying it to #22532. The accepted objective silently drifts: reviewers and git history record approval of 'cache status' while the artifact quietly includes unrelated webhook tooling; running the script from any directory other than scripts/ creates or edits a .env in an unintended parent directory.

[ADVISORY] The dev:cron runner is swapped from ts-node to npx tsx (line 10), a dev-tooling change unrelated to the calendar-cache feature the PR promises. Feature reviewers sign off on a build-tooling change they were never asked about; and when tsx is not present in node_modules/.bin, npx fetches an unpinned version from the registry at dev-runtime instead of using the repo's pinned toolchain.

[BUG] The dropdown renders the destructive 'Delete cached data' action for delegation credentials (hasCache is evaluated independently of canDisconnect), but deleteCache.handler.ts requires userId: user.id on the Credential, which org-owned delegation credentials never satisfy. An org member whose Google connection is a delegation credential sees 'Delete cached data' whenever a CalendarCache row exists for the delegation credential id; every click sends deleteCache with that credentialId, the handler's findFirst({id, userId: user.id}) returns null, and the mutation throws — the user permanently gets the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast for an action the UI keeps offering. Either the UI must gate the cache section on canDisconnect or the handler must support delegation credentials; as written the feature is dead for exactly the org-delegation scenario the cache feature targets.

[BUG] The handler signals the expected not-found/forbidden outcome by throwing a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, which tRPC converts to a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR response rather than a 4xx. Both legitimate failure cases — a stale credentialId after the credential was disconnected, and a probing/foreign credentialId — surface as HTTP 500 server errors, polluting error monitoring with expected client outcomes as apparent server faults and denying clients a distinguishable 404/403 to react to; the onError toast path in CredentialActionsDropdown can't differentiate 'gone' from 'server broke'.

[ADVISORY] The only test-infrastructure change in this diff — a hardcoded `return []` mock of getCacheStatusByCredentialIds — verifies none of the new server behavior: no spec in the diff exercises deleteCacheHandler (including its credential-ownership branch), the groupBy→_max.updatedAt mapping in CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId, or the connectedCalendars cache-status enrichment (the diff contains no files matching spec/**, test/**, __tests__/**, *.test.*, or *.spec.*; the only test-adjacent files are this mock and scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, a manual dev script with no assertions). Destructive/authz regressions ship green: deleting the `userId: user.id` filter in deleteCache.handler.ts:20 lets any authenticated user delete another user's calendar cache, and swapping `_max` for `_min` in the groupBy silently reports the wrong 'Last updated' timestamp — neither is caught by any test.

[ADVISORY] The new 157-line CredentialActionsDropdown — the `!canDisconnect && !hasCache → return null` gate, both destructive confirmation flows, and the delegation case where only cache actions render — has no test, and the shipped CalendarCacheRepositoryMock hardcodes `[]`, so mock-backed environments can never produce a non-null cacheUpdatedAt that reaches the hasCache branch. A regression that renders the dropdown for every credential (breaking the delegation/disableConnectionModification guarantee the old inline DisconnectIntegration conditional enforced) or that fires deleteCache with the wrong credentialId passes CI; the cache-status UI path is untestable with the mock as written.

[ADVISORY] The new `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` sits outside the cache-miss `if`, so every fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache call — including calls served entirely from a still-valid cache — performs an UPDATE across all SelectedCalendar rows of the credential, and the mechanism relies on Prisma auto-bumping @updatedAt from an empty `data: {}` payload, which nothing in the diff verifies. Availability/booking-page lookups that previously hit a valid cache with zero writes now incur a multi-row DB write per call (amplified by the user's selected-calendar count), and if SelectedCalendar.updatedAt lacks @updatedAt the feature silently does nothing — no test distinguishes either case.

[BUG] deleteCache.handler throws a plain `Error` instead of a TRPCError, so the expected not-found/foreign-credential outcome surfaces as HTTP 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a 4xx (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN). Users hitting the legitimately-expected failure (stale UI pointing at a deleted credential, or a credential they do not own) generate 500s that pollute error monitoring as server faults, and API consumers cannot distinguish client error from server failure.

[BUG] `sed -i '' -E …` is BSD/macOS-only syntax; on GNU/Linux sed parses `''` as an (empty) script and the substitution expression as an input filename, so the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL line is left unchanged while the script still prints '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL'. A Linux developer running this webhook test-setup script silently tests against a stale or absent GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL — Google webhooks never reach the tunnel while the setup appears configured.

[BUG] `hasCache` ignores `delegationCredentialId`, so a delegation Google credential with CalendarCache rows renders the 'Delete cached data' action, but deleteCache.handler's ownership check (`userId: user.id`) can never match a delegation credential, so the action always fails. Members with delegated Google calendars see a 'Delete cached data' menu item whose every invocation returns the 'Error deleting cache' toast — a permanently broken action shipped in the UI (the same component correctly gates disconnect on delegationCredentialId but not delete-cache).

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendars.handler constructs `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of resolving through the ICalendarCacheRepository seam whose mock this same diff updates, so the mock's new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is unreachable on this path and cache-disabled environments (where the mock logs 'Skipping … due to calendar-cache being disabled') execute a real Prisma groupBy on every connectedCalendars fetch. Operators running with calendar-cache disabled get an extra DB query per connectedCalendars call, and test authors cannot substitute the mock for this path — the interface/mock pair updated in this diff is dead code for the feature it was updated to support.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache.handler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` directly, bypassing the ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential method that already exists in the interface and mock, duplicating cache deletion outside the seam this diff maintains. Cache-deletion logic now lives in two places (repository and handler); the disabled-mode skip implemented in the mock never runs for this mutation, and any future change to deletion semantics (e.g., also resetting the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump) must be made twice or the paths drift.

[ADVISORY] `updatedAt: true` and `googleChannelId: true` are added to the user's selectedCalendars select (and to the UserWithCalendars Pick type in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts) but no code in this diff reads either field — the connectedCalendars enrichment sources cacheUpdatedAt from the CalendarCache table instead. Every user fetch through this repository pulls two unused columns and the type contract widens for no consumer; readers cannot tell whether SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is meant to back the cache-status UI (it is not — CalendarCache.updatedAt is), which is exactly the ambiguity the unverified updateManyByCredentialId bump depends on.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", …)` inside an otherwise fully localized component (every surrounding string goes through t()). Non-English users see US-style dates (e.g. '7/15/25, 3:04 PM') for the cache status while the rest of the page follows their locale; Cal.com's localized date-formatting utilities were bypassed.

[BUG] The freshness signal added in this PR bumps SelectedCalendar.updatedAt on every availability fetch, but the cache-status UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, so the two halves of the feature never connect and the new write is dead with respect to the display it was added for. Every booking-page availability check now performs an extra unconditional UPDATE of all SelectedCalendar rows under the credential (write amplification and row-lock contention on the hottest read path in the app) with zero effect on the displayed 'Last updated' value, which only moves on actual CalendarCache rewrites, not on the refreshes this code signals.

[BUG] Delegation-credential entries (canDisconnect=false) that have CalendarCache rows render the 'Delete cached data' action, but deleteCache.handler's findFirst requires userId = session user id and delegation credentials have userId null, so the mutation always throws for them. The user confirms a dialog promising deletion and always receives the 'Error deleting cache' toast plus a 500 in server logs — a permanently dead action offered by the UI for every delegation-based Google connection with cached data.

[ADVISORY] DEFAULT NOW() backfills every pre-existing CalendarCache row with the migration-run timestamp, which the new UI then presents as that cache's actual last-updated time. Immediately after deploy, every existing Google connection with cached data shows 'Last updated: <deploy time>' — a fabricated freshness value that persists until that row's next cache rewrite, misrepresenting cache age to users.

[ADVISORY] updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the SelectedCalendar select here (and mirrored into the UserWithCalendars picks in packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts) but no code in this diff consumes either field. Dead payload fields shipped in every connectedCalendars response and two extra select/type sites to keep in sync on the next change; they also corroborate that the freshness signal was wired to SelectedCalendar while the status UI reads CalendarCache (see the CalendarService finding).

[ADVISORY] deleteCache.handler throws a plain Error for the expected not-found/not-owned case, which tRPC converts to a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a 4xx TRPCError. Every expected authorization failure (including the delegation-credential dead end) is logged and paged as a server error, and the client receives an indistinguishable generic failure instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code it could act on.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler throws a plain Error("Credential not found or access denied") for an expected not-found/authorization failure, which tRPC converts to a 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a 4xx TRPCError (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN). A user who clicks 'Delete cached data' on stale UI state (credential already revoked elsewhere) gets a server-error response for an expected client mistake; in production the error formatter strips the plain-Error message so the client cannot distinguish causes, and every such user error is recorded as a 5xx, polluting server-error monitoring and alerting.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query — unlike the sibling disconnectMutation in the same file, which invalidates it in onSettled — and relies solely on the optional onSuccess prop to refresh the cache status. After a successful cache deletion the dropdown keeps rendering the stale 'Last updated' timestamp and the 'Delete cached data' item (hasCache stays true) until an unrelated refetch, so users re-run the delete on already-deleted data; hosts that do not pass onSuccess never see the UI update at all.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository with `new` instead of resolving it through the selection that swaps in CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar-cache is disabled — the shipped mock implements this exact method as a 'Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled' no-op, which only makes sense as a runtime disabled-mode path. On deployments running with calendar-cache disabled, every connectedCalendars fetch now executes a real CalendarCache groupBy that the disabled path exists to skip, and cache-status behavior silently diverges from the disabled-mode contract the rest of the calendar-cache feature follows.

[ADVISORY] The SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bookkeeping write runs unguarded after the availability data has already been fetched and persisted to CalendarCache, so a failure in this non-essential updateMany throws out of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache and fails the whole availability operation whose real work already completed. adjudication.rationale: The new `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` uses `sed -i '' -E ...` to update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` (line in diff under the `if grep -q '^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL='` branch).
